description: Create a reusable inventory data hook that fetches all cars and adds cars through the existing GraphQL API. It must own query/mutation state and update the inventory when a mutation succeeds.
acceptance: Uses the existing GET_CARS and ADD_CAR GraphQL operations.
Exposes inventory data plus fetch loading/error and add loading/error states.
Adding a vehicle updates the inventory data after the mutation succeeds without requiring a page reload.
Does not issue GraphQL operations from presentation components.

description: Build the card presentation for a single vehicle, including responsive image source selection for the specified phone, tablet, and desktop width bands.
acceptance: Displays the vehicle make, model, year, colour, and photograph using the existing component library.
Uses the phone image at widths up to 640px, the tablet image from 641px through 1023px, and the desktop image at 1024px and above.
Uses responsive image markup so unsuitable larger sources are not requested for smaller viewports.

description: Build the inventory controls for entering a model filter and choosing whether to sort by year or make.
acceptance: Provides a model filter that updates as the user types.
Provides sort choices for year and make.
Uses controls from the project's existing component library.

description: Build the add-vehicle form as a presentation component with required-field validation and submission status feedback.
acceptance: Collects make, model, year, and colour and passes them to the supplied submit callback.
Prevents submission when any required value is empty or the year is missing or invalid.
Shows submission progress and a plain mutation error when supplied by the inventory page.
Uses form controls from the project's existing component library.

description: Build the inventory page that coordinates data state, filtering, sorting, responsive card layout, and the add-vehicle form while delegating GraphQL access to the reusable hook.
acceptance: Consumes the reusable inventory hook rather than issuing GraphQL requests directly.
Shows an in-progress state while the initial inventory request is loading and a plain error message if it fails.
Filters cars by case-insensitive partial model text and then sorts the filtered result by the selected year or make option.
Renders every resulting vehicle as a card in a layout that adapts to phone, tablet, and desktop widths.
Submitting a valid vehicle through the form calls the add operation and allows the returned vehicle to appear in the inventory.

description: Wire the inventory page into the application and provide it with the project's existing GraphQL client.
acceptance: Renders the inventory page as the application screen.
Provides the existing Apollo client context required by the inventory hook.
Contains only application wiring, not vehicle presentation or data-access logic.

description: Add an automated test proving that inventory loaded from the mock API is rendered after the initial loading state.
acceptance: Runs through the project's existing mock GraphQL API rather than a live network.
Confirms a loading indication is shown before the inventory response arrives.
Confirms returned vehicles render as cards with their make, model, year, colour, and photograph.

description: Add an automated test proving that typing a partial model name filters the inventory displayed from the mock API.
acceptance: Runs through the project's existing mock GraphQL API rather than a live network.
Typing part of a model name narrows the rendered inventory to matching models as the user types.
Matching is verified without requiring exact casing or a complete model name.

description: Add an automated test proving that year and make sorting reorder the inventory and operate on the currently filtered list.
acceptance: Runs through the project's existing mock GraphQL API rather than a live network.
Selecting year changes the displayed vehicle order by year.
Selecting make changes the displayed vehicle order by make.
Sorting while a model filter is active preserves that filter.

description: Add an automated test proving that valid vehicle details are submitted through the mock API and the created vehicle appears immediately, while empty submission is rejected.
acceptance: Runs the add mutation through the project's existing mock GraphQL API rather than a live network.
Entering make, model, year, and colour and submitting causes the new vehicle to appear in the inventory without reloading the page.
An empty form does not submit an add mutation.
